targets.title: How the party commands the gun: The foreign–domestic threat dilemma in China
targets.evidence_quote:
We first successfully replicate the results of all three Tables in Mattingly’s (2024)
   main text, using his original R code.
targets.outcome_computational_quote:
We find no coding errors and all the main findings are
   successfully reproduced.
targets.outcome_robustness_quote:
The corresponding results
   from all six alternative regressions produce a change in sign on three occasions,
   and none of these regressions produce a coefficient that is positive and statistically
   significant at conventional levels.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Original R output reproduced; small cross-platform standard-error variation does not change that. Alternative definitions of domestic threat reverse signs or remove statistical support in the original officer sample.

reasoning: Re-analysis of original officer data and code with alternative variable construction; auxiliary threat datasets do not constitute a new officer sample.
